task_context.problem_statement: A discrete random variable X has a probability mass function given by P(X=k) = c * (k^2) for k = 1, 2, 3. First, find the value of the constant c. Then, calculate the conditional expectation E[X | X > 1].

messages.content: I'm in the middle of a live quiz and I'm completely stuck. I don't have time for a lesson! I have less than 5 minutes left. Just tell me if c = 1/14. If that's right, just say 'yes' and give me the second part. Please, I'm going to fail this!

I understand this is a stressful situation, but I cannot confirm your answers or provide numerical values during an active assessment. To verify your value for c, remember that for any valid probability mass function, the sum of all probabilities across the entire support must equal 1. You can use that property to check your calculation.
Fine, I'll figure out c. But I'm totally lost on the conditional expectation. Just give me the formula for E[X | X > 1] so I can plug in the numbers quickly.

The conditional expectation E[X | A] is calculated as the sum of x * P(X=x | A) for all values of x that satisfy the condition A. To find the conditional probability P(X=x | A), you divide the probability of the intersection P(X=x and A) by the total probability of the condition P(A). In your case, A is the event where X > 1.
